newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-KRAJICEK STRUGGLES TO REACH THIRD ROUND IN WINDY TOKYO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KRAJICEK STRUGGLES TO REACH THIRD ROUND IN WINDY TOKYO.

text.p: Wimbledon champion and top seed Richard Krajicek struggled to beat unseeded South African Neville Godwin and windy weather in the second round of the $1.22 million Japan Open on Wednesday.

Dutchman Krajicek, still licking his wounds after being thrashed in the second round of last week's Indian Open by newcomer Andrei Pavel of Romania, blamed his problems on the windy conditions in Tokyo.
"I really thought it was a struggle. In the last three games I was serving very well but it was very windy out there," he said. "I had the feeling I was battling every point."
Krajicek said Godwin, who beat Pavel in Tuesday's first round, had a good return of serve.

"He must have hit 10 or even more winners off my second serve," Krajicek added after his 6-3 6-4 victory. "My game suits his game a lot. He's not someone who can create a lot of speed by himself but he likes the way I play when I give him a target."
Krajicek, 25, faces Magnus Norman in Thursday's third round after the Swede beat American Justin Gimelstob 6-4 6-2 on Wednesday.
Women's sixth seed Naoko Sawamatsu, still visibly troubled after twisting her ankle on Tuesday, had a long battle to overcome Japanese compatriot Mana Endo 6-1 4-6 6-4 on Wednesday.
Sawamatsu faces American third seed Amy Frazier in Thursday's third round.
